What is our primary use case?

I am currently working in the Maestro Flow and IXP. In a booking, we get and combine the documents and consolidate a lot of data from multiple systems. We extract the data using the IXP and populate the data in the Action Center for human review. Once the human review is complete, another agent runs for the transformation. After transformation is done, it goes to the end system. This process involves humans, agents, and all system data together, which really reduces the manual effort of users from getting data from multiple systems. The human in the loop helps users validate the data before it goes into the end system.

Currently, the solution is related to Maestro and IXP. IXP is effective because it extracts data from various document types. Maestro is very useful because I can track all instances in Maestro. Whenever the process fails, I have the feature to retry and also edit any variables that have been used. This is one of the good things I have seen recently.

Document understanding with IXP is valuable because previously I had to train and annotate documents extensively, but now it is a matter of writing prompts. If you are skilled enough to write a prompt, you can extract the data. In our particular use case, we receive multiple types of documents with no certain limit on templates. We might receive over 150 templates of documents, but we need to extract the same fields from all of them. The ideal way with traditional document understanding would not work because I cannot train the document since I cannot collect that many types of documents. It is very hard to annotate, train and test.

However, with IXP, I just upload the document, write a clear and precise prompt without overloading the model, and annotate and validate how it is working. Based on that, I can manipulate and adjust. There is also significant time saving in terms of training and extraction. I can handle various numbers of templates. In our case, there are no certain templates available. There can be any templates, but the data needs to be extracted correctly, and this depends on who is writing the prompt. This is really helpful.

Maestro is as useful as always. If a transaction is failing in the middle of any process, I can directly retry. I do not have to spend time starting from the beginning. Assume this is one of the biggest projects I am working on, which involves 10 processes. If it is failing in the 10th process, I do not have to run it from the first. The 10th process might have failed because of some application login issue or the application might be in maintenance mode. However, when I want to retry, I can directly retry.
